nodes.text: and the other leader holds the glade.' Having spoken thus, with frozen
features, and Bacchus now departing from her, she fell silent.
But trembling at the portent and unequal to his many terrors,
the king, the help of the long-lived seer and the knowing darkness
of Tiresias (the custom of those who fear what is uncertain), sick at heart
It swiftly seeks the heights and, like a falling thing,
rises the other way, and at last, spent, from on high
returns more slowly to the earth and sinks into the field.
So falls, whenever she is torn from the astonished stars,
the Sun’s darkened sister; far off, the peoples clash helping
bronzes and fear in vain, but the victorious Thessalian
laughs at the panting pair of horses once her spell is heard.
The Danaans applaud, but to you, as you watch, it is no comfort,
Hippomedon, and a mightier arm is hoped for on equal ground.
Tisiphone. And now, her father won over, Tritonia
had come, and was bringing undying glory to the wretched man,
and him, soaked with the gore of the shattered brain,
she sees, polluting his jaws with living blood
(and his comrades cannot take it from him): the fierce Gorgon stood erect,
the throngs, wrapped [in it]; and first, having stolen the light arrows
from the bold boy's back, she fills with heavenly
shafts his quiver, of which not one without blood
falls; then she sprinkles his limbs with ambrosial liquid,
sprinkles his horse, so that his body be not violated by a wound
before his death, and she mingles sacred chants and knowing
murmurs, which she herself, in secret caves, teaches the Colchian women
by night, showing the wild herbs to those who seek them.
Then indeed, with bow bared, he flies around, all fire,
and does not govern himself by reason; of his country, his mother and himself
